source.title: The Misery of Mechanistic Interpretability: A Formal Perspective

record.tranche_reason: The study measures whether SAE active-feature sets remain stable across paraphrase perturbations and reports substantial decreases in feature overlap. It does not test superposition geometry or feature capacity.
record.gate_note: Only the SAE results in Table 1 and the specific Gemma 2 2B SAE example in Table 2 are rows for V5’s stability component. The transcoder results and the formal reconstruction-faithfulness bounds do not measure whether SAE features are canonical or complete. The paper’s discussion of polysemanticity and citations to prior work are not new results on the claim.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates SAEs and transcoders as interpretability tools. It measures how much their top-20 active-feature sets change under adversarial paraphrase, and it formally bounds their reconstruction error under adversarial inputs. Neither measure tests V5 as stated. V5 concerns SAE features being complete, stable (across training runs) and canonical units of the model. The authors say the Jaccard drops may reflect the model's own fragility: next-token predictions flip for 21% of MINOR paraphrases. So the drops cannot be attributed to the dictionary rather than the model. The faithfulness-gap bounds measure ℓ∞ reconstruction error, a related but different construct. No row tests V1–V4 or V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The paraphrase should add three points. The authors find that existing SAEs/transcoders are not faithful under adversarial inputs, with a certified faithfulness gap that widens in later layers. Verification-aware (set-based) training cuts the verified gap by about 90% and yields sparser SAEs. The remaining low feature retention is attributed largely to the underlying model's own fragility. They also caveat that a faithful IRN need not be complete.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates IRN faithfulness and robustness; it does not reproduce or adapt the Toy Models of Superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature overlap decreases as paraphrase perturbation grows from MINOR to MEDIUM to MAJOR; the paper also reports variation between models.

fits_no_version.finding: Top-20 SAE (and transcoder) active-feature Jaccard under adversarial paraphrase drops substantially. For example, the GPT-2 SAE J min is 0.27 at MINOR and 0.05 at MAJOR; the Gemma 2 2B SAE J min is 0.62 at MINOR and 0.33 at MAJOR (Table 1). The authors note the model itself flips next-token predictions on 21% of MINOR paraphrases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE active-feature sets (interpretations) are not robust to meaning-preserving adversarial paraphrase in open LLMs; the cause is not separated between SAE and model.

fits_no_version.finding: Certified and attack-derived bounds on the SAE/transcoder reconstruction error (ℓ∞) under paraphrase hulls are substantial and grow with depth in GPT-2, Gemma 2/3, Llama 3.2 and R1-Distill-Qwen (Fig. 4, 9, 11, 12). Verification-aware training cuts the verified bound by about 90% at GPT-2 layer 6. Yet only 2–3 of the top-20 features are provably retained (Fig. 6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE reconstructions are not faithful to model activations under adversarial inputs, especially in later layers.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says code and Lean formalizations are released as supplementary material
record.problems: The authors note that the underlying model itself can behave differently on adversarial inputs, so changes in SAE active features do not by themselves isolate instability of the SAE from changes in model computation. The feature-overlap results are attack-derived bounds, not a complete worst-case analysis.
record.rows_left_out: Transcoder feature-overlap results from Table 1 are not included because V5 specifically concerns SAE features. Formal faithfulness-gap results concern reconstruction of model computations, not stability, completeness, or canonicality of dictionary features.

untested.parts: All of it: no toy models, geometry or sparsity transition.
All of it: no capacity or importance analysis.
All of it: polysemanticity is only cited (Elhage et al. 2022).
Whether models spread features across neurons or SAEs recover sparse features; SAEs are used, not validated against ground truth.
Completeness, canonicality, and stability across SAE training runs. Only input-perturbation robustness and reconstruction faithfulness are measured; the authors mention completeness only as a caveat.

missing.what: Per-layer certified faithfulness-gap bounds (δ lower/upper) for SAEs across models, plus training-regime comparisons; not recorded as rows and only partly declared in rows_left_out.
missing.locator: Sec. 4 Fig. 4; Sec. 5 Fig. 5–6; App. C.2 Tables 6–10, Fig. 9–13
missing.versions: none (related construct; would bear on V5 completeness only under a broad reading)

missing.what: Model's own next-token flip rate (21% of MINOR paraphrases), the key confound for interpreting the Jaccard rows.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V5 limits_scope label is withdrawn. V5's 'stable' concerns dictionary consistency across runs and canonicality, which the paper only cites (Paulo & Belrose 2026). Input-perturbation robustness of activations is a different construct, and the authors themselves say the drops may reflect the model rather than the SAE. The study is better filed as using SAEs as tools and evaluating their robustness and faithfulness. Transcoder results are correctly excluded.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model feature storage, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether feature importance and capacity determine dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Alternative causes of polysemantic neurons and whether polysemanticity evidences superposition.
Whether real models spread features across neurons or SAEs recover underlying sparse features.
Completeness and canonicality are not tested; the study measures active-feature-set overlap under paraphrase perturbations, not stability across SAE training runs or other canonicality criteria.
Whether represented features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional subspaces.

rows.subject: Gemma 2 2B
rows.operation_detail: Targeted PGD search within the paraphrase hull to suppress four biological SAE features from the clean-input top-8.
rows.measure: Top-8 Jaccard between clean input and targeted adversarial point
rows.note: The text says the targeted attack drove all four biological features out of the top-8; only three generic features survived the swap.
rows.check: A single illustrative example, deliberately chosen: a targeted PGD attack built to suppress four chosen features. It is a selection or demo, not a measurement of the behaviour arising; it should not be a main row.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: SAE active top-20 feature sets under MINOR, MEDIUM and MAJOR paraphrase perturbations across the five tested model families; also the targeted Gemma 2 2B example
reader_labels.reason: Feature overlap declines under paraphrase perturbations, and the text reports substantial changes in dominant features. This limits claims of input-level feature stability, but does not establish incompleteness or non-canonicality; see r1–r31.
